_about: Phosphor's own paths and the exceptions, for db_watch.py. 'protected': a pattern (fnmatch, or re: a regular expression) and why a file there matters. 'expected': files a database may install there because Phosphor deals with them (the main distribution's Main and menu core, swapped for Phosphor's; MiSTer Linux, behind the Linux update warning). 'var_ids': Update All settings in status.json and the databases they switch on. 'catalog' (by title, then database id) and 'catalog_prefix': each database's category (cores, special cores, hybrid cores, wallpapers, bios, game art, tools, not needed) and tag (ok, patch, launcher, warn, block, in phosphor, not needed, opt-in, review), with why; for patch and launcher, 'ready' says whether Phosphor's parts exist yet and 'parts' which files Phosphor deals with: 'phosphor:<file in Phosphor's release>' (Phosphor's file goes in its place: same path, Phosphor's hash and URL, so MiSTer's downloader installs and keeps it) or 'original' (installed as it comes, not used by Phosphor). The rest come from the original database. A part is never just removed: the downloader would delete the file as obsolete.
